title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197302
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1973 July: South Vietnam grants first oil concessions to foreign firms. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 45; NSZGSZHS 213; Hayton, The South China Sea, 71; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 19). Eight contracts were awarded.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197303
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1973 July 12:  South Vietnamese destroyers bring personnel and materials to support construction/long-term occupation on Namyit Island (鸿庥). (NSZGSZHS 119, 221). AMTI says it was 1974.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197304
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1973 Fall: South Vietnamese government publishes map, including the Paracels in South Vietnam's territory (NSZGSZHS 213). Frst time? Needs checking.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197305
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1973 September: South Vietnam formally annexes 10 islands in the Spratly Islands to protect oil exploration, deploying hundreds of troops on Namyit Island. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 71). NSZGSZHS indicates late 1973 or January 1974, and maybe 11 features? (NSZGSZHS 17, 119).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197306
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1973, November: South Vietnam rams Chinese fishing boat, detains crew, and forces them to confess that the Paracels belong to Vietnam. (盘点中国历次反击战：人民日报发完社论后开打 http://www.peacehall.com/news/gb/z_special/2012/05/201205130534.shtml -- see also Benson, "South China Sea").

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197401
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1974 January 18: South Vietnamese foreign minister tells the United Nations that the Paracel and Spratly Islands are Vietnamese territory. The language employed is  similar to modern Chinese rhetoric on the South China Sea. Claimed sovereignty to the UN again in March. (不可分割的一部分，这一事实是明显的, 不可否认的) (NSZGSZHS 214). On January 29 the South Vietnamese military command releases revised injuries and death count from the battle that month: in the two days battle, one ship was sunk and three damaged (unclear which side this is referring to).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197402
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1974 January 30 to February 8, 17-20: South Vietnam occupies various features in the Spratly Islands. Occupies or strengthens presence on Nanwei, Nanzi, Dunqian, Jinghong, and erects a sovereignty marker on Anbo. Also starts construction. Reports claim between 4-7 features. (NSZGSZHS 20, 119-120, 222-224; Chen Jie PhD, p.151; AMTI). March 30: South Vietnam publishes the names of the 5 islands it is occupying in the Spratly Islands (or at least 5 new ones?):  Nanwei (南威岛), Skylark/Yunque [云雀] (判敦谦沙洲), Shuangzixi [双子西] (南子岛), Shengcun [生存] (景宏), and Nanxie [南歇] (鸿庥岛) (NSZGSZHS 115-124).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197403
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1974 February: Spike in rhetorical assertions of sovereignty over the Paracel and Spratly Islands by South Vietnam, including expressions of willingness to use force to gain complete control over the island groups. (NSZGSZHS 216-217).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197404
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1974: Major hydrocarbon developments launched by South Vietnam. First geophysical surveys of Phu Khanh Basin and Nam Con Son Basin (no PetroVietnam data) (H. Luong Lien, The Economics of Petroleum 1998 Exploraiton, 6.26). In August first wildcat wells (oil) drilled in Nam Con Son Basin (Hong 1, Block 12E). (H. Luong Lien, The Economics of Petroleum 1998 Exploraiton, 6.6-6.7) Pecten discovers first oil and gas in Nam Con Son Basin (Dua 1, Block 12E). (H. Luong Lien, The Economics of Petroleum 1998 Exploraiton, 6.17)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197501
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975, early: Southwest Cay incident, in which South Vietnamese troops occupy Philippine-held Southwest Cay while its garrison was at a party on neighbouring Northwest Cay. A few months later Southwest Cay becomes the first target of North Vietnamese troops when they arrive (Hayton, South China Sea, 101-102).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197502
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975 February 14: South Vietnam publishes a white paper, reaffirming its clam to sovereignty over the Spratly Islands (NSZGSZHS 120; Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 46 dates this White Paper to April 1975).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197503
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975 April-May: Vietnam takes control of South Vietnamese possessions in the Spratly Islands. NSZGSZHS says various points in April, Garver says April, Do Thanh Hai says May, a different reference book says May, and Dzurek says April. (NSZGSZHS 115-124, 203-207; Garver; NSZGSZHS 115-124; other reference book?; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 19).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197504
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975 May 5-6: “the delegation of the Provisional Revolutionary Government in South Vietnam to the Colombo Meteorological Conference requested the World Meteorological Organization to continue to recognise Vietnam’s meteorological station, No.48.860, on the Hoang Sa Islands and opposed China’s registration for its station there.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 48).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197505
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975 August: Victorious North Vietnam issues resolution outlining guidelines for oil and gas exploration throughout the country. "It identified the continental shelf off the southern coast and the Tonkin Gulf in the South China Sea as priority exploration areas" (ICG, Oil in Troubled Waters, 11).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197506
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975 September 25: “After reunification, Hanoi departed from its customary passive position, openly asserting Vietnam’s sovereignty over the Paracel and Spratly archipelagos. In an official meeting on 25 September 1975, Vietnamese party chief Le Duan officially raised the status of the Paracel and Spratly Islands with Chinese Vice Premier Deng Xiaoping.” Followed up with a forceful note in November. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 48).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197508
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1975, presumably late in the year: Vietnam builds airstrip on Spratly Island (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 48; NSZGSZHS 47-48).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197601
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1976: Vietnamese forces on Southwest Cay fire on nearby Philippine aircraft (Van Pham, "Use or Threat of Force," 525).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197701
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1977 May 12: Vietnam unilaterally issues “Statement on the Territorial Sea, Contiguous Zone, Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf.” Followed up in 1982. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 52; Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao").

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197801
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1978 March-April: Vietnam occupies multiple features in the Spratly Islands. Features include Shuanghuang Shoal/Bank (双黄沙洲), Ranqing Shoal/Bank (染青沙洲), Nailuo Reef (奈罗礁), Zhong Reef (中礁). Vietnam also entered and planted flags at Zhubi (渚碧) Reef, Changxian Reef (长线礁). Vietnam also entered two unnamed [redacted??] islands (Vietnamese names provided: Yuchuan Island [渔船岛] and Pangrong Island [潘荣岛], with a sovereignty marked erected on Yuchuan). (NSZGSZHS 121-122; 203-207).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197801
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197802
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1978, April 26: Vietnam Central TV broadcasts first Spratly documentary, indicating that its maritime consciousness struggle is already in progress. The documentary emphasizes how "these islands belong to Vietnam, Vietnamese people's footprints appeared long ago in these remote islands". (Zhang, NSQDDSJ, 63).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197803
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1978: first geophysical survey of Song Hong Basin (no PetroVietnam data). (Lien, "The Economics of Petroleum," 6.27).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN197901
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1979 April 10: Vietnam deployed 3 ships of soldiers to conduct reconaissance within 500 meters of [Chinese possessions in?] the Paracel Islands, allegedly provoking Chinese forces by shooting. Apparently not the only recent provocation of this nature, and these provoctions are taking place amid Sino-Vietnamese negotiations (NSZGSZHS 36-38; Garver, "China's push")

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198001
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1980, Feb: Vietnam holds military exercises in Spratlys (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao")

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198002
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1980 July: Vietnam and the Soviet Union sign an agreement on the cooperative exploration and mining of oil and natural gas in Vietnam's continental shelf (NSZGSZHS 40; Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ, 88; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 18) In 1985 the Soivet Union and Vietnam sign a long term oil exploration and production plan, part of a broader plan to expand Vietnam's energy production (NSZGSHS 352-355). Partnerships with USSR were likely inherited by Russia.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198101
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1981: energy development intensifies with first magnetic and gravity surveys of Nam con Son Basin and Song Hong Basins (Lien, "The Economics of Petroleum," 6.28).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198201
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1982, February: Vietnamese ships detain Guangzhou trawlers fishing in the Paracels. China retaliated by capturing a Vietnamese vessel (Garver 1992, 1008; Fisheries Yearbook 2000, 269).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198202
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1982 June: Vietnamese navy second in command (越南海军一副司令) inspects the Spratly Islands (NSZGSZHS 122). These sorts of visits continue regularly, one or two visits every few years, into the early 1990s, at least to 1993, and then again in 2003.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198203
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1982 November 12: Vietnamese government publishes statement on territorial seas baseline (NSZGSZHS 41, 122; Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ 93-94; Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 52).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198301
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1983 November 12: Vietnam and the Soviet Union collaborate to use Ilyushin-18 (伊尔-18型) aircraft to atmospheric survey in the Spratly Islands (NSZGSZHS 122).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198702
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1987 (onward): Offering of offshore oil concessions to foreign companies, including in disputed areas. "After the Foreign Investment Law was promulgated at the end of 1987, the government opened up offshore areas for petroleum exploration to foreign companies." The following year Vietnam published its expansive oil and gas blocks map covering areas claimed by all other claimants. (VN MOFA spokesman statement, April 20, 1994, reprinted in Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ 253).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198801
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988 February 20: Vietnamese foreign ministry spokesperson demands that Chinese ships investigating (考察) and patrolling the Spratly Islands leave or "accept full responsibility for the consequences" (撤离并扬言要中国对"所引起一切后果承担全部责任"). (NSZGSZHS 45)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198802
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988: Mobilization of population before and after South Johnson Reef skirmish. the whole country surging with anti-China waves" (在全国上下掀起反华浪潮), mobilizing the masses of every sphere to assist Vietnam's operations in the Spratlys (NSZGSZHS 46). Do Thanh Hai notes that after China takes Cuarteron Reef, Vietnam begins internal mobilization of groups like the Youth Union and Vietnam Lawyer’s Association (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 50).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198803
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988 March-April on: major international PR campaign, with Vietnam making strong efforts to convince the United Nations that the Spratly and Paracel islands belong to Vietnam and that China provoked the skirmish on Johnson South Reef (NSZGSZHS 54-55, 56-59). UN efforts are aided by Cambodia (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 50-51)

publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198804
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988 March-May: post-skirmish occupations and construction by Vietnam in the Spratly Islands. PLA tells reporters that after the 3-14 incident, Vietnam occupied Qiong Reef (琼) and Guihan Reef (鬼喊). AMTI confirms that these two reefs were indeed occupied in 1988. PLA alleges that Vietnam has built up forces on the newly occupied (1988) islands and reefs, including Daxian (大现), Nanhua  (南华), Liumen  (六门), Wumie (无乜), Riji (日积), and Dong Reef (东) (NSZGSZHS 54-55).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198805
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988 April - June: Vietnamese moves to shore up its existing positions in Spratly Islands after the Johnson South Reef skirmish. In April thirty Vietnamese ships are deployed to Spratly Islands to block further Chinese expansion. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 51). May: Vietnam's Defense Minister Le Duc Anh visits the Spratlys to inspect troops and vow to defend Spratly Islands, and Vietnamese Navy conducts live-fire exercises. (Wen Hui Bao, quote Garver 2009; Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 51).

publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988 June: Vietnam sends 150 "construction workers" to Spratlys to construct barracks on one island. (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ 163).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198807
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1988 onwards: Offshore oil development agreements signed with foreign oil companies covering disputed areas. "Since 1988, more than 30 production sharing contracts have been signed with foreign oil companies"  (Lien, "The Economics of Petroleum," 6.20). Between 1988 and 1994: “Vietnam Oil and Gas Corp., which reported directly to the prime minister, signed twenty-seven production-sharing agreements to allow foreign oil groups from dozens of countries to explore its offshore blocks.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 96). Practice of signing such agreements has continued to the present.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198901
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1989 January 14: VN holds awards ceremony for individuals and units involved in defending Spratlys (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ, 178)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198902
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1989: PRC repeatedly criticises Vietnamese detentions of PRC fishers (Chen, "China's ASEAN policy," p.179). Implicitly this may have continued at least until 1994, when another similar case is identifiable.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN198903
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1989 August: DK-1 rig building in Nam Con Son Basin commences. "In August 1989 Vietnam built facilities on Bombay Castle (on Rifleman Bank), Vanguard Bank, and Prince of Wales Bank, bringing to 24 the number of islets and reefs under its control." (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 22). August 19: China criticizes Vietnam's commencement of construction of an economic and scientific and technical service complex in the Truong Sa archipelago (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao"; VAFIS, "Sovereignty.").

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199001
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1990, May 17: VN MOFA spokesman reads statement to the Mixed Committee of the UNESCO Oceanography Program saying China's Spratly scientific research activities are violating Vietnam's sovereignty & territorial integrity (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ 190).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199002
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1990 (onward): Vietnam significantly increases pace of drilling (wildcat wells), lasts at least through the 1990s (Lien, "The Economics of Petroleum," 6.12). According to a 1998 source, although offshore exploration drilling began in 1974, 78.4% of all wildcats were drilled after 1989. (Lien, "The Economics of Petroleum," 6.20).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199101
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1991: Vietnam builds DK-1 platforms on Alexandra Bank and Grainger Bank (Vuving, "South China Sea: Who Occupies What"). AMTI confirms.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199201
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1992, June 27: Vietnamese state news agency reports Vietnam has built small fishing harbour on Spratly Island. (Zhang NSQDDSJ 230). PRC codemns in September 1994 (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute 33; KYODO - 'China says Vietnam port encroaching on its waters').

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199202
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1992 May-June: Vietnam strongly protests Crestone's oil exploration, submitting a note to the United Nations (Hayton 2014). VN has regularly used UN channels to denounce PRC actions since; indeed this policy could be traced back as far as 1988.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199202
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1992 May-June: Vietnam strongly protests Crestone's oil exploration, submitting a note to the United Nations (Hayton 2014). VN has regularly used UN channels to denounce PRC actions since; indeed this policy could be traced back as far as 1988.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199203
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1992, Sept 4: Vietnam summons PRC ambassador to protest and demand removal of a survey ship and drilling ship from Gulf of Tonkin. Reuters describes this as the toughest statement against Chinese actions since February. (Zhang NSQDDSJ, 233) On September 5: “Hanoi even warned Beijing of the possibility of using force to ward off two Chinese vessels exploring for oil in the Gulf of Tonkin.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea 80).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199204
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1992 October 18: Vietnam sends meterological and resource survey team to Spratlys (Zhang NSQDDSJ 235)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199301
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1993 March onwards: Vietnam takes a series of measures retaliating against PRC moves over WAB-21 and Gulf of Tonkin. Vietnam approves Mobil involvement in "Blue Dragon" development and in December 1993 explore in Block 5.1b within the 9DL, near Crestone concession, though not overlapping (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao"; Fravel 2008, 297; Hayton 2014). Crestone's Thompson was invited to Hanoi for meeting with PetroVietnam, who offers him joint venture in return for cancelling CNOOC deal. Thompson declined (Hayton 2014). A month after accusing PRC of resuming oil exploration in the Gulf of Tonkin in September 1993, Vietnam invited oil companies to bid on nine offshore blocks, including contract areas around Vanguard Bank and Prince of Wales Bank within the PRC WAB-21 block. "On 19 April Mobil signed a production-sharing contract with PetroVietnam for Block 5-1b (Blue Dragon)." And "north of the Crestone area, PetroVietnam and Nopec offered offshore licenses in Vietnamese blocks 122-130." (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 28-30). This offering by PetroVietnam was reported on November 12: ""Nine tracts are involved, designated blocks 122-130 and covering more than 60,000 sq km extending from southeastern waters to the central part of the South China Sea which Hanoi prefers to call its Eastern Sea. To ensure interest from foreign oil companies, Petrovietnam is sweetening its production sharing terms and, for the first time, staging "road shows", or promotional seminars. The offshore tracts opened for tender are described as "frontier" and are largely unexplored, mainly because they lie in deeper waters and in the disputed area claimed by China. However, Nopec international marketing and business development manager Halfdan Castens says the lower blocks may have potential for oil and the northern part may be gas-prone. However, an executive of a British oil firm operating in the country doubted Vietnam would be successful in luring western oil firms into the troubled and deep waters. According to Nopec, water depths range from near-shore to more than 2,000 metres. Nopec's Castens stressed not all blocks were in disputed waters." (International Gas Report, via Taffer dataset)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199302
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1993 April: Vietnam sending civilian immigrants to Spratlys, according to Vietnamese media interview with D/PM 陈德良 who recently inspected there. The D/PM was quoted by Vietnam's military paper (via Xinhua, via Yomiuri Shimbun) as stating, "On these [five] islands there is already an immigration program . . . in order to unify economic tasks and national defense objectives, [we] must strengthen economic activities and civilian activities." (Zhang NSQDDSJ 246). According to one PRC source, Vietnamese immigration to Spratlys began in late 1980s, encouraged by preferential policies such as low- or no-interest loans to buy boats, and the development of infrastructure such as schools (Zhang NSQDDSJ 257-9).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199303
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1993 Aug 7: "On 7 August Vietnam provided an export tax exemption for fishing in the Spratly islands." Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 28). On June 4, 1994 Vietnamese authorities make Spratly aquatic products tax-free (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao").

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199303
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1993 Aug 7: "On 7 August Vietnam provided an export tax exemption for fishing in the Spratly islands." Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 28). On June 4, 1994 Vietnamese authorities make Spratly aquatic products tax-free (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao").

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199304
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1993 Nov: New Vietnam lighthouse on Southwest Cay (Nanzi). (Zhang, NSQDDSJ 265; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 29).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199401
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1994 May-June - June 1995: Lighthouse-building project expands  in Spratly Islands. Vietnam builds 42m lighthouse on Ladd Reef, and 22m lighthouse on West Reef, 30nm from Ladd Reef (Nansha, "Nanhai Zhudao"; Zhang, "Appendix II").

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199402
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1994 April-August: Vietnam escalates in response to Crestone tensions. In April a naval incident involves a Chinese vessel carrying out seismic research for Crestone and Vietnamese vessels ordering it to quit an area considered by them to be under Vietnamese jurisdiction. The Chinese vessel may have followed the order. (FEER October 13, 1994, quoted in VAFIS, "Sovereignty").  "During May or June 1994 PetroVietnam began to drill in Vietnam’s block 135, which is within Crestone’s concession from the PRC." (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 28-30). Rig is VietSovPetro's Tam Sao, and the move prompts a two-month standoff with PRC ships (Hayton). In August armed vessels from Vietnam confront Crestone & Chinese company's collaborative drilling in Van An Bac (Blocks 133-135) (Vietnam.vn, "Chronicle of major events")

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199402
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1994 April-August: Vietnam escalates in response to Crestone tensions. In April a naval incident involves a Chinese vessel carrying out seismic research for Crestone and Vietnamese vessels ordering it to quit an area considered by them to be under Vietnamese jurisdiction. The Chinese vessel may have followed the order. (FEER October 13, 1994, quoted in VAFIS, "Sovereignty").  "During May or June 1994 PetroVietnam began to drill in Vietnam’s block 135, which is within Crestone’s concession from the PRC." (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Dispute, 28-30). Rig is VietSovPetro's Tam Sao, and the move prompts a two-month standoff with PRC ships (Hayton). In August armed vessels from Vietnam confront Crestone & Chinese company's collaborative drilling in Van An Bac (Blocks 133-135) (Vietnam.vn, "Chronicle of major events")

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199403
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1994,  July 8: Vietnam 9th National Congress 5th Session passes UNCLOS motion claiming Paracels and Spratlys.PRC MFA spokesperson Shen Guofang denounces, says China is ready to shelve disputes and jointly develop. (RMRB p. 4 外交部发言人举行记者招待会 重申中国对西沙和南沙群岛的立场) National assembly had authorized ratification of UNCLOS on June 23. (Vietnam circulates report on UNCLOS implementation; Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 75).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199404
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1994 July 2: Vietnam seized three Chinese fishing boats and detained their crews (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 31). China protested [stern representations] the Vietnam's seizure and demanded the return of the vessels and the crew.  (MID 3.0 narratives #4030) Was in Gulf of Tonkin acc. MFA spokes Shen Guofang (Zhang Liangfu NSQDDSJ, 265) Sources in Taffer dataset concur.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199405
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1994, late: Vietnam started oil production in two more fields, Dai Hung (Big Bear) (Block 05– 1) and also at the ostensibly undisputed Rong (Dragon) (Block 16). (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 96).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199501
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1995, early: Vietnamese construction follows the PRC occupation of Mischief Reef.  "On 28 February Vietnam announced that it had reinforced its Spratly outposts." (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 37; see also Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 84-85).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199502
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1995, June: Lighthouse-building expands into Malaysian claimed area as Vietnam also "inaugurated" a new lighthouse on Amboyna Cay in June 1995. (Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 38).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199601
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1996 April: Energy development agreements with third-country oil companies in new areas. "Vietnam asserted its UNCLOS rights, authorising a consortium led by Conoco Vietnam Exploration and Production BV, a unit of Houstonbased Conoco Inc., to explore Blocks 133 and 134, which encompassed three million acres of the South Con Son basin, about 200 miles off Vietnam’s southern coast. These offshore acreages were also situated within Tu Chinh area (Vanguard Bank) that overlapped with the northwestern part of the South China Sea area China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) and Crestone referred to as Wan’an Bei-21 (WAB-21; see Figure 2.10). As compared with its production-sharing agreement with Mobil Oil in 1994, Hanoi’s Conoco enterprise made an even deeper inroad into the WAB-21 area that China claimed.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 95; Dzurek, The Spratly Islands Disupute, 42).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199701
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1997 March: First use of ASEAN to push back against PRC, following the PRC's Kantan-03 oil rig move. On March 20 "in an unprecedented move, Vietnam’s Deputy Foreign Minister Vu Khoan met with the ambassadors of seven ASEAN members to inform them of the oil-drilling dispute and explain Vietnam’s position. The day after, Hanoi held a press conference to condemn China’s violation of its EEZ and continental shelf.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 99).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199801
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1998 January: “Vietnamese soldiers fire on a Philippine fishing boat near Vietnam-controlled Tennent (Pigeon) Reef, injuring a Filipino fisherman.” (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force in the South China Sea Disputes, 527; "Philippines Lodges Protest Over Shooting in Spratlys," Deutsche Presse-Agentur, January 19, 1998)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199802
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1998 July-August: New DK-1 platforms at Orleana (Aonan) and Kingston (Jindun) Shoals (Chen Qi, "Expansion and Military Deployment; Fravel, Strong Borders, 298); Vietnam constructs “two economic-scientific technological service stations in the Spratly Islands (Ba Ke reefs)"; China protests. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 101).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199901
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1999 October: Vietnamese forces allegedly fire warning shots at Philippine aircraft flying over Vietnam-controlled areas of the Spratly Islands. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 101; Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force in the South China Sea Disputes, 528; "RP Protests Viets Firing at Place," Manila Standard)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN199902
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 1999: In ASEAN preparations for drafts for a code of conduct in the South China Sea, Vietnam advocates for the Paracel Islands to be included in the Code, which some other ASEAN parties disagreed with. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 111). Continues pushing for this until Declaration of Conduct in 2002. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 116; (Storey 'Trouble and strife…')

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200101
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2001: "China reacted angrily when Vietnam set up a local government in the Spratlys similar to other administrative districts in the country." (Vietnam celebrates claim to Spratley islands). "on February 10 [Vietnam] claimed to establish a "local government" in the Spratly Islands to "facilitate administration", "never give up an inch of land", and "will not hesitate to fight." (Sina via Taffer dataset).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200201
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2002 August: “Vietnamese troops fire warning shots at Philippine military reconnaissance planes circling over Spratlys.” (Van Pham, The Use or Threat of Force in the South China Sea Disputes, 529; Tran Dinh Thanh Lam, "Bird Watchers, Divers, Tourists Ignite Spratlys Row,” Asia Times Online).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200301
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2003, April-June: When China sent a scientific research ship to the Spratlys, "Vietnamese navy sent ships to constantly monitor it, impeding China's normal scientific research activities" (NISCSS 2003 report, 36). Internal PRC source.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200401
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2004 April: Spratly tourism commences. Vietnam “announced a controversial plan to open a boat tour for civilians to one of the Spratly Islands, which it described as ‘normal civilian activity.’” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 126). First tour on April 19 with 100 tourists. (SOA Memo 2004; China irks…; China indignant…; Zhang, "Appendix II") Boat tours have continued to the present.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200402
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2004 onward: Depletion of fish stocks in Vietnam’s coastal areas and China-Vietnam Gulf of Tonkin fisheries agreement pushes Vietnamese fishermen further out into the South China Sea. Increased presence of Vietnamese fishing vessels in Paracel Islands, resulting in more incidents with Chinese fishery administration vessels. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 137).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200403
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2004: Infrastructure upgrades in Spratlys.  Vietnam begins modernizing Spratly Island runway (CSIS 2017, 237), and on May 29 Vietnam Posts and Telecommunications Corporation announces it will use a satellite link to provide Internet service to soldiers in the Spratlys. (Internet to play role in islands spat)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200404
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2004 September: PetroVietnam offers nine offshore blocks to international oil firms in the Phu Khanh Basin in the central/south part. “It should be noted that almost all previous offerings were in the Song Hong Basin in the north and Cuu Long Basin and Nam Con Son Basin in the south.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 136; Vietnam rejects China's Spratly oil…; NISCSS 2004 report p.13) Signing of PSCs over these blocks (122-128) would become targets of PRC coercion from 2006 (KNOC, "Vietnam Acreage")

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200601
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2006 June-July: Chinese survey ships carrying out seismic work south of the Paracels allegedly "fended off waves of Vietnamese “armed vessels” (武装船) sent to obstruct the survey." (Martinson, The Arming of China's Maritime Frontier, 7-8). Happened in June 2007 as well as 2010 and 2014, so arguably an ongoing line of behavior through that period.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200602
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2006, June 16: India's ONGC Videsh signs up for Blocks 127 and 128. "In 2006, ONGC Videsh, an Indian state-owned oil exploration corporation, obtained permission from Vietnam to explore several blocks (including 127 and 128) in the South China Sea in waters also claimed by China" (ICG, Oil in Troubled Waters, 12, KNOC, Vietnam Acreage Map). This broadened the disputed area covered by contracts with third-country oil companies.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200701
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2007: Continental Shelf surveys ahead of UNCLOS deadline, which continue through 2008 (Wikileaks cables). Only China appears to have objected.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200702
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2007, April: Vietnam elevates Truong Sa (Spratly Island) to the level of a “township” under the Truong Sa District. (Swaine & Fravel, "China's Assertive Behavior," pp.15-16)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200703
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2007 August 6: “Vietnam officially demanded the US ocean drilling company, Transocean, to cancel its concession agreement with CNOOC for Block 2-4 west of the Paracel Islands, which overlapped with Vietnam’s Block 141.” [response to oil tensions] (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 141). Also: “Since 2007, Vietnamese officials repeatedly asked their US counterparts to pay more attention to the East Asia and particularly to dissuade the US companies from dropping their projects in the waters offshore Vietnam.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 182).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200704
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2007 December: Vietnam’s first ever public demonstrations about the South China Sea. (Hayton, The South China Sea, 151, 153). Subsequent cases were seen in 2008, 2011 and 2014.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200801
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2008, January: "China accused Vietnamese fishermen of attacking Chinese trawlers in the Gulf of Tonkin. Vietnam responded that Vietnamese and Chinese fishing boats had merely bumped into each other after getting their nets entangled." (Storey 'Trouble and strife…'). Jan 17 2008: "China has asked Vietnam to seriously investigate a recent robbery of some of its fishing vessels by Vietnamese fishermen in the Beibu Gulf. "China is highly concerned about the case, and has made representations to Vietnam and required the Vietnamese side to seriously investigate and handle the case, and at the same time, take effective measures to avoid further cases," said Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Jiang Yu at a regular press conference here on Thursday." (Xinhua via Taffer database).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200802
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2008, July: Vietnam signs preliminary cooperation agreement with US company Exxon Mobil to explore disputed areas in the southern and central coastal areas. (NISCSS 2009 report p.11). 2008, early: Exxon signs MOU with PetroVietnam to explore Blocks 156-159. "The blocks were by far the furthest offshore that Vietnam had ever leased. The south-eastern corner of Block 159 was more than 500km from the Vietnamese coast – well into disputed territory. ExxonMobil was also in serious talks about leasing Blocks 117, 118 and 119 just off Vietnam’s central coast." (Hayton 2014)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200803
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2008: Vietnam's diplomatic lobbying efforts stepped up. Vietnamese opposition forced a Swiss offshore drilling company to cancel a Paracels contract with China (CSIS 2017, 204). Also in 2008 Vietnam managed to lobby IOC to remove China's 9-dash-line in the official online map of the Olympic torch relay (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 157).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200804
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2008: Vietnam's domestic public opinion campaign stepped up. The Vietnamese government urges mass media and press to launch propaganda to raise public awareness of Vietnam’s sovereignty over Paracels and Spratlys. “We must assert absolute sovereignty over the country’s land and waters to maintain stability and peace for growth,” noted President Nguyen Minh Triet, who had a working session this week with the army forces of Military Zone No5, the patrol unit of sea and waters including Hoang Sa and Truong Sa." (Vietnam News Brief Service via Taffer dataset). Late 2008 saw further “Major changes in Vietnam’s information policy in the maritime domain...New instructions from CPV’s Central Commission for Publicity and Education on 2008 November 26, followed by a succession of state-funded nation-wide propaganda campaigns, a propaganda conference on the SCS in March 2009 in Hai Phong. Much more media coverage and critical public discussion followed. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 158-160).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200805
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2008 (late) onward: In addition to domestic information policy changes, Vietnam also steps up more international outreach to advance its position such as Track II workshops, and protests by Vietnamese scholars against inclusion of 9-dash-line in various publications (e.g. Google Maps, National Geographic, Science) (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 160-163; also "Swaine & Fravel, China's Assertive Behavior," 16).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200901
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2009, early April: Vietnam gives 21 families living in the Spratlys a deposit book with 5 million dong, and officially commissions Chairman of Hoang Sa County People’s Committee. (NISCSS 2009 report, p.12).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200902
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2009 May 6 and 7: Vietnam presents joint submission with Malaysia on its southern continental shelf to the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf, and a partial report on its northern continental coast. (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 171).

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200903
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2009 May (onward): Vietnam intensifies opposition to China’s extended unilateral fishing ban. The Vietnam Fishery Association continues to encourage fishermen to sail off with the purpose of “both doing business as usual and asserting Vietnam’s sovereignty and jurisdiction,” and “When the fishing boats were captured, Hanoi issued protests through the statement of the MOFA spokespersons and diplomatic notes, and worked through bilateral channels with Chinese authorities to secure their release.” (Do Thanh Hai, Vietnam and the South China Sea, 174-5)

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200904
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2009, Sept 21-22: Vietnamese ships "shadow and harrass" USNS Victorious in SCS. (WIKILEAKS #09HANOI895) Location unknown, but perhaps most likely to have occurred around Vietnam's straight baselines encompassing Con Son Island, as Vietnam's "excessive straight baselines" are noted as a target in the DoD's 2009-2010 FONOP report.

title: MATS 1.02 case description, VN200905
publisher: Chubb, A. (2022), "Maritime Assertiveness Time Series (MATS 1.0)" dataset, version 1.02
excerpt: 2009 onwards: Land reclamation and other infrastructure upgrades in the Spratlys.
